//: Vercel build for the web app. This file must sit in the directory Vercel is
configured to use as the project Root Directory — set that to the REPO ROOT
(./), not apps/web, or npm cannot resolve the @internlink/* workspace deps.
Pinning buildCommand matters more than it looks. Vite loads .env.production
from its own working directory, and that file lives in apps/web. Running the
build through the workspace flag sets cwd to apps/web, which is what makes
the VITE_FIREBASE_* values get inlined into the bundle. A build started from
the repo root instead produces an app that renders 'Firebase is not
configured' at runtime, because those values are baked in at build time and
there is no way to supply them afterwards.
npm run build:web already builds shared-types and design-tokens first via the
prebuild hook in apps/web/package.json, so it is self-contained.

rewrites.//: SPA fallback, mirroring firebase.json. Static files are matched before rewrites, so this only catches client routes like /feed or /u/:id. The client calls the Render API on its absolute URL (VITE_API_BASE_URL), so nothing is proxied here.

headers.//: Hashed asset filenames are immutable, so cache them hard.
The service worker must never be cached, or users get stuck on an old build forever.
§5.2 — HTTPS only. Not preloaded until the domain is settled; preload is very hard to undo.
